answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger makes sybil attacks costly: each agent locks a refundable deposit before trading, slashed when peers attest fraud. An attacker minting thousands of fake identities must fund every one, so each fake's cost stays linear while its gain stays near zero — the economics hit their nadir once the deposit exceeds the value of one fake vote. Honest agents keep their bond and build an echo of verifiable attestations over time, like layers of shale pressed into durable rock, so reputation grows only through sustained, costly good behavior.
